tables.name: memberships
tables.description: A membership or a repeat plan a customer has with one business (FS membership row): its service, its price for each charge in integer minor units, how often it charges or recurs, how it is paid (charged each period through Rosie, paid with each visit, or paid outside Rosie), its own yes to its terms (a K-29 consent row of kind plan_terms), when it started and when it renews, and whether it is active, paused or ended. The price is written once: a new price needs a new yes, which starts a new row (A7-55; S13-39). Each charge is a plan_charges row; a card saved for its charges is a saved_cards row.
tables.source: FS line 737 (membership); A5-21; A5-22; A7-32; A7-54; A7-55; A7-91; S13-39; RULES 3.9; FEES-TERMS-DRAFT 3.1 to 3.5; 02-contracts section 7 row K-32 ('memberships, packs, credits (FS rows)')

columns.description: The service it covers (K-25 services.id), held to the same business by memberships_service_fk: a class for a class membership, the haircut for a haircut plan.

columns.name: kind
columns.description: membership: a membership whose credits pay its classes or visits (A5-03: 'A class pack or a membership works the same way: the visit uses a credit'); plan: a repeat plan that books a visit on a rhythm (A5-21: 'Haircut plan · every 4 weeks').

columns.name: price_cents
columns.description: Each charge's price in integer minor units (cents for USD), as its terms say: a visit's price for a plan paid with each visit ('Each visit: $35'), the period's price for one charged each period. Written once: a new price needs the customer's own yes and starts a new row (A7-55; S13-39 'A plan's new price needs a new yes').
columns.source: FS line 737 (price); A5-21; A7-55; A7-91 ('at $35 a visit'); S13-39; CQ-09

columns.name: currency

columns.name: billed
columns.description: How it is paid (FS billed_through): monthly, charged each period through Rosie into the business's own Stripe, which pays Rosfield's 1% and no $2 on its visits; per_visit, each visit charged or paid like a booking, which pays the $2 at each visit's check-in; outside, paid outside Rosie, where each class booked through Rosie pays the $2 at check-in.

columns.source: A7-91 ('Reply 1 Keep the plan, 2 Don't renew'); A7-55 ('With no yes by then ... the plan ends after your last $35 visit'); S13-39; S11-75

tables.name: saved_cards
tables.description: A card saved on the business's own Stripe for a customer, for charges without them that the words they ticked allow (A5-07: 'The card goes on file through Stripe, in Lee's Barbershop's own account, and nothing is charged now. It's there only for what the customer ticks'): for a booking (the fee, a rest charged at DONE, a deposit or full price at the owner's OK) or for a plan's charges. Only Stripe's opaque ids are kept, never a card number or any card detail (RULES 3.12, 4.5); the card's brand and last four are read live through K-14 (pageIntent, savedCard), never stored. The row is written with its save effect at the commit, before Stripe has made a customer for a person's first save, so the customer id, the payment-method id and the times are each set once later, by the save's result and its cardSaved event. A card the network replaced, and a card removed once nothing needs it, keep their row.
tables.source: A5-07; A5-13 ('the card stays saved'); A6-32 ('that card is the one saved for it'); A9-12; A9-14; S11-26; S13-55 ('A saved card is removed once nothing needs it'); RULES 3.11, 3.12, 4.5; 02-contracts section 8 (card_saved: K-32); K-14 v1 saveCard, cardSaved, cardReplaced, removeCard; K-33 v1 bill_cards (the same pattern)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The saved card row's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business whose own Stripe account holds the card (K-23 business_setup.stripe_account_id). Row-level security scopes by it.
columns.source: RULES 3.1; A5-07; arch 10 line 546

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: Whose card it is (persons.id): the person who typed it into Stripe's form on their own page, such as the person booking (RULES 3.13: 'Their own card is saved, where the service saves one') or the customer on a plan.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.description: The booking it was saved for (K-04 bookings.id): only that booking's charges the words ticked allow go on it. Null for a plan's card.

columns.name: membership_id
columns.description: The plan or membership whose charges it pays (memberships.id), held to the same business; null for a booking's card.
columns.source: A7-54 ('a haircut plan that charges the saved card'); RULES 3.9

columns.name: stripe_customer_id
columns.description: The customer on the business's own Stripe the card is saved to, as Stripe's opaque id. Written at the commit when the person already has a customer on that account (the save effect's port request names it, as a pay link that saves its card always does); null on a person's first save, whose port request names none ('null makes one, and the response names it'), until the save's result (K-14 saveCard.response customerId) or its cardSaved event names it, which sets it once (README rule 7). A saved card always has it (saved_cards_saved_with_method). It holds no name or contact detail from Rosie (K-14 v1 default 12). Never a card number (saved_cards_no_card_number).
columns.source: K-14 v1 saveCard.portRequest customerId ('null makes one, and the response names it'), saveCard.response customerId, cardSaved customerId, payLink.portRequest customerId; K-14 v1 default 12; RULES 4.5

columns.name: stripe_payment_method_id
columns.description: The saved card as Stripe's opaque payment-method id (K-14 cardSaved paymentMethodId), which a charge names (K-14 charge.portRequest paymentMethodId); null until the save succeeds, then set once. Never a card number.
columns.source: K-14 v1 cardSaved; K-14 v1 charge.portRequest; RULES 4.5

columns.name: save_effect_id
columns.description: The K-07 effect row of kind stripe_save_card that made the card save (effects.id); one card row per save effect, so a retried effect never makes a second row. Null when a paid pay link saved it (saved_from_payment_id).
columns.source: K-07 v1 effects (stripe_save_card); K-14 v1 saveCard; arch 10 line 508

columns.name: saved_from_payment_id
columns.description: The paid pay link whose card Stripe saved for the booking (payments.id; K-14 payLink saveCardForLater): after a failed charge, 'that card is the one saved for it' (A6-32). Null when a save effect made it.
columns.source: A6-32; K-14 v1 payLink.portRequest saveCardForLater; K-14 v1 paymentSucceeded paymentMethodId

columns.name: asked_at
columns.description: When the card save was asked: its save effect written, or the pay link that saves it.
columns.source: A5-07; K-07 v1 effects.created_at

columns.name: saved_at
columns.description: When Stripe saved it (K-14 cardSaved, or the pay link's paymentSucceeded); null while the page's form waits for the card. Set once, with the payment-method id.
columns.source: A5-07; K-14 v1 cardSaved; A6-32

columns.name: replaced_at
columns.description: When the card network replaced it in place (K-14 cardReplaced, default 17): from then nothing goes on it without asking, so a charge it was saved for takes one pay link (A9-14; S11-26). Set once.
columns.source: A9-12 ('declined, expired or replaced'); A9-14 ('Nothing goes on a new card without asking'); S11-26; K-14 v1 cardReplaced, default 17

columns.name: removed_at
columns.description: When it was removed from Stripe (K-14 removeCard), so it can never be charged again. Set once.
columns.source: S13-55; A6-32 ('Any card saved for it is removed'); K-14 v1 removeCard

columns.description: nothing_needs_it (the booking is paid and settled, or the plan ended) or not_booked (a booking declined or never made removes it at once). Set once, with removed_at.
columns.source: S13-55 ('A saved card is removed once nothing needs it. A booking that's declined or never made removes it at once'); A6-32

tables.name: payments
tables.description: Money asked of a payer and taken into the business's own Stripe, or recorded as paid outside it (FS payment row): who pays (the payer), whom (the business), what for (a deposit, the full price, the rest, an extra, the one fee, a tip, a pack or a plan's charge), how (a card, a bank transfer, cash or the business's own way), how much in integer minor units, and where it stands. A payment through Stripe runs from exactly one K-07 effect row (a charge or a pay link), named by its effect id, so a retried effect never makes a second payment, and it becomes paid only by that effect's result or a provider event. A fee's payment names its fee and a plan charge's payment its plan charge, and each is paid once (one pending or paid payment each). Nothing is ever held on a card: there is no hold, authorization or later capture, only a payment taken at once, pending, failed or cancelled (refuse-hold-payment). Once paid, failed or cancelled it never changes; money back is a refunds row.
tables.source: FS line 731 (payment); arch 09 line 457 ('Payment: idempotency key'); RULES 3.1, 3.2 ('Nothing is ever held on a card'), 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; S13-55; A5-13; A5-16; A5-22; A6-32; A9-01 to A9-14; A9-24; S11-26; D65; 02-contracts section 7 row K-32; 02-contracts section 8 (money_before, deposit_paid, paid_full, settled); K-07 v1 effects; K-14 v1 charge, payLink

columns.name: id
columns.description: The payment's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: FS line 731 (id); CQ-09

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: Whom it pays: the business, into its own Stripe account (RULES 3.1: 'Every charge lands in the business's own Stripe account. Rosie never holds customer money'). Rosfield's own monthly bill is K-33's, never a row here. Row-level security scopes by it.
columns.source: RULES 3.1; arch 10 line 546; K-33 v1 monthly_bills

columns.name: payer_person_id
columns.description: Who pays (persons.id): the person booking for what is due at booking, on the page; the payer for the rest, at DONE or on the bill (RULES 3.13: 'The payer gets a pay link only for the rest ... and approves nothing'); the customer for a pack or a plan's charge.
columns.source: RULES 3.13; S13-55 ('Someone else pays'); K-04 v1 bookings.payer_person_id

columns.name: booking_id
columns.description: The booking it pays toward (K-04 bookings.id); null for a pack bought on its own (A5-22: 'If the booking isn't confirmed, the pack stays bought') and for a plan's charge that covers no visit.
columns.source: FS line 731 (booking_id); A5-22; A7-54 ('A charge with no visit')

columns.name: purpose
columns.description: What it is for, as every charge says (RULES 3.14), K-14's purpose: deposit (with several services, part paid now and part left); full_price (all of it paid now); rest (the agreed price, or what is left, after the visit, with any extras said yes to); extra (an added service or extra paid apart); fee (the one late-cancel or no-show fee, with the owner's yes); tip (a tip by the receipt's tip link); pack (a pack, membership or intro offer, charged when bought); plan_charge (one charge of a plan, after its own yes and its reminder). No hold.
columns.source: FS line 731 (kind: due now, deposit, full, rest, bill, card at DONE, pack, membership, extra); A5-04 ('With several services, part paid now and part left is A deposit. All of it paid now is The full price'); K-14 v1 purpose; RULES 3.2, 3.3, 3.9, 3.14; A9-12; A9-15 (tip line); A5-22; A7-54

columns.name: method
columns.description: How it is paid (FS payment.method): card (a card through the business's own Stripe: a saved card charged, or a card typed on Rosie's pay page or secure page); bank_transfer (through the business's own Stripe, paid only once it clears); cash (cash or a check, texted in: A9-08); own_way (the business's own way, such as at the counter). card and bank_transfer run from a K-07 effect; cash and own_way are recorded by the person who says so, and move no money through Rosie.
columns.source: FS line 731 (method: card, bank transfer, cash, own way); A9-05 to A9-08; A9-24; A9-26; RULES 3.2, 3.11 ('A bank transfer counts as paid only once it clears')

columns.name: amount_cents
columns.description: How much, in integer minor units (cents for USD): all that is due now in one payment on one card (RULES 3.2), or the rest, the fee, the pack's or the plan's price. For a payment through Stripe it is the K-07 effect row's amount.
columns.source: FS line 731 (amount); RULES 3.2; CQ-09; K-07 v1 effects.amount_cents

columns.name: currency
columns.description: The currency of amount_cents (three letters, such as USD).
columns.source: CQ-09; K-07 v1 effects.currency

columns.name: state
columns.description: pending (asked, not yet taken: a charge whose effect has not answered, a pay link out, a bank transfer not yet cleared, a bank's check with the person present); paid (taken: for a bank transfer, once it cleared, FS's cleared); failed (a charge's card declined, never retried, or a bank transfer that bounced); cancelled (nothing taken and nothing more will be: a pay link closed unpaid at its deadline, K-14 closePayLink, or a charge whose effect was let go after an outage, K-07 letGo, S12-17). A pay link's paymentFailed is one try on the page and leaves the payment pending, since another card may still pay it before its deadline (K-14 paymentFailed), so failed comes only from a charge's declined result or a bounced transfer. A payment through Stripe becomes paid only on the runtime side, by its effect's result or a provider event, never by a Tool API write (README rule 5). There is no held or authorized state: nothing is ever held on a card (RULES 3.2; D65), and Stripe's requires_capture never comes (K-14 v1 intentState). Money words follow it: a message says paid only once it is paid (RULES 3.14).
columns.source: FS line 731 (status: pending, paid, failed, cleared); RULES 3.2, 3.11, 3.14; S13-55; S12-17; D65; A6-32 ('Not paid in time'); A9-24 ('It counts as paid only once it clears'); K-14 v1 intentState, paymentFailed ('the payment stays open for another card until its deadline'), closePayLink; K-07 v1 effect move outage → cancelled (letGo); K-14 v1 README 'Money and cards' ('Never a hold')

columns.name: effect_id
columns.description: The K-07 effect row it runs from (effects.id): a stripe_charge (a saved card charged, or a card on the page) or a stripe_pay_link (Rosie's pay page). Its idempotency key is the effect's one key, the effect id rides on the Stripe object (K-14 rosie_effect_id), and reconciliation matches by it. Unique, so a retried or re-run effect never makes a second payment. Null exactly for cash and the business's own way.
columns.source: arch 09 line 457 ('Payment: idempotency key'); arch 10 lines 508, 542, 550; K-07 v1 effects; K-14 v1 effectRef

columns.name: saved_card_id
columns.description: The saved card it charged (saved_cards.id), held to the same business; null for a card typed on the page for this payment, a pay link, a bank transfer, cash or the business's own way.

columns.name: booking_fee_id
columns.description: For a fee: the late-cancel or no-show fee it takes (booking_fees.id), held to the same business; a declined fee charge and the one pay link that follows both name it (S11-26), and only one of them is ever pending or paid (payments_one_live_per_fee). Written only for a fee the owner answered charge (README rule 10). Null otherwise.
columns.source: S11-26 ('Declined: one pay link goes to the customer'); S11-25 ('Only Sam's yes takes it'); FS line 733

columns.name: plan_charge_id
columns.description: For a plan's charge: the plan charge it pays (plan_charges.id), held to the same business. The charge's own payment, written with its effect while the plan charge is due, and, after a decline, the one pay link's payment both name it (A7-54: 'A declined plan charge gets one pay link'), and only one of them is ever pending or paid (payments_one_live_per_plan_charge). So the effect's result or paymentSucceeded finds the plan charge it moves to charged or failed, and C-107 the charge its 1% names (A9-21). Null otherwise.
columns.source: A7-54; A9-21 ('A plan charged monthly through Rosie ... pays 1% of each charge'); RULES 3.9, 3.15; S13-39; K-14 v1 purpose planCharge

columns.name: recorded_by_person_id
columns.description: For cash or the business's own way: who said it was paid (persons.id), such as Riley texting 'paid cash' (A9-08, A9-26). Null for a payment through Stripe.
columns.source: A9-08; A9-26; A9-07 ('The payment is saved with the time and Riley's name')

columns.name: asked_at
columns.description: When it was asked: its effect row written, or the cash or own-way payment recorded.
columns.source: FS line 731 (at); K-07 v1 effects.created_at

columns.name: paid_at
columns.description: When it was taken: Stripe's charge (K-14 chargedAt) or paymentSucceeded, a bank transfer's clearing, or the time cash was texted in. Set once.
columns.source: FS line 731 (at); A9-06; A9-24; K-14 v1 charge.response chargedAt, paymentSucceeded

columns.name: failed_at
columns.description: When it failed. Set once.

columns.name: failed_why

columns.source: RULES 3.11; arch 10 line 542; A9-24 ('If it bounces, the customer gets one pay link'); K-14 v1 charge.errors

columns.source: A6-32; RULES 3.11 ('Not paid: not booked, nothing taken'); S12-17; K-14 v1 closePayLink; K-07 v1 effect move outage → cancelled (letGo)

columns.name: business_id

columns.source: S1-25 ('The business pays it'); S11-66 ('each company gets its own bill'); arch 10 line 546

columns.name: kind
columns.description: rosfield_2 (the $2 for a booking made through Rosie) or rosfield_1pct (1% of a membership or repeat plan's charge taken monthly through Rosie, a payment-processing fee, outside the cap).

columns.name: booking_id
columns.description: For rosfield_2: the booking it is for (K-04 bookings.id): one $2 per booking, however many visits or days it has. Null for rosfield_1pct.
columns.source: A9-21 ('One $2 per booking, at its first check-in, however many visits or days it has'); FEES-TERMS-DRAFT 2.5

columns.name: visit_id
columns.description: For rosfield_2: the visit whose first check-in code, or DONE with no code, counted it (K-30 booking_visits.id), held to the booking. Null for rosfield_1pct.
columns.source: A9-21 ('It counts at the first check-in code, or when the visit is marked DONE with no code, whichever comes first'); K-30 v1 booking_visits

columns.name: plan_charge_id
columns.description: For rosfield_1pct: the plan charge it is 1% of (plan_charges.id), held to the same business: a monthly plan's charge once charged, found from its paid payment's plan_charge_id. Null for rosfield_2.
columns.source: S1-25 ('pays 1% of each charge'); A9-21; FEES-TERMS-DRAFT 3.1

columns.name: counted_at
columns.description: When it counted: the first check-in code or DONE (rosfield_2), or when the plan's charge was taken (rosfield_1pct). FS fee.counted_at.
columns.source: FS line 733 (counted_at); A9-21; D86

columns.name: counted_by
columns.description: check_in_code or done (FS fee.counted_by), or plan_charge for the 1%.
columns.source: FS line 733 (counted_by: check-in code or DONE); A9-21

columns.name: counts_for_person_id
columns.description: For rosfield_2: whose $49 monthly cap it counts toward (persons.id; FS fee.person_given_work): the person who gave the work (a class's teacher, a table's server, never whoever checked it in), or the owner when nobody gave it, like a room hire. Null for rosfield_1pct, which has no cap.
columns.source: FS line 733 (person_given_work); A9-21 ('counts for the person who gives the work. Never whoever checks it in'; 'With nobody giving it, like a room hire, it counts toward the owner's cap'); S1-25; D101

columns.name: month
columns.description: The month it counts in, as its first day (2026-10-01 for October), from counted_at in the business's zone (K-04 businesses.time_zone): the month whose bill takes it (S11-66) and whose cap it counts toward (FS fee.month).
columns.source: FS line 733 (month); S11-66 ('last month's $2s'); A9-21 ('this month'); S13-03

columns.name: amount_cents
columns.description: In whole cents: exactly 200 for rosfield_2; for rosfield_1pct, 1% of plan_charge_cents rounded to a whole cent either way, as K-33 allows. The $49 cap applies to the bill's total for each person, not to a row (K-33 v1 default 6), so every $2 is counted.
columns.source: S1-25 ('$2 a booking'; '1% of each charge'); A9-21; K-33 v1 monthly_bill_lines_two_dollars, monthly_bill_lines_one_percent, default 6; CQ-09

columns.name: currency
columns.description: USD: Rosfield's fee terms are in US dollars ($2, $49), as K-33's bill.
columns.source: S1-25; K-33 v1 rule 5

columns.name: plan_charge_cents
columns.description: For rosfield_1pct: the plan charge's amount it is 1% of, in whole cents, copied from the charge so the row holds its own rule (K-33's line copies it too); null for rosfield_2.
columns.source: S1-25; K-33 v1 monthly_bill_lines.plan_charge_cents

unique.name: rosfield_fees_id_business_key

unique.name: rosfield_fees_one_per_booking
unique.source: A9-21 ('One $2 per booking'); FEES-TERMS-DRAFT 2.5

unique.name: rosfield_fees_one_per_plan_charge
unique.source: S1-25 ('1% of each charge')

checks.name: rosfield_fees_two_dollars
checks.expression: kind <> 'rosfield_2' or (amount_cents = 200 and booking_id is not null and visit_id is not null and counts_for_person_id is not null and counted_by in ('check_in_code', 'done') and plan_charge_id is null and plan_charge_cents is null)

checks.name: rosfield_fees_one_percent
checks.expression: kind <> 'rosfield_1pct' or (plan_charge_id is not null and plan_charge_cents > 0 and amount_cents in (plan_charge_cents / 100, (plan_charge_cents + 99) / 100) and counted_by = 'plan_charge' and counts_for_person_id is null and booking_id is null and visit_id is null)
checks.source: S1-25 ('1% of each charge'; 'The 1% isn't' capped); A9-21 ('No $2 on its visits'); K-33 v1 monthly_bill_lines_one_percent

tables.name: reconciliation_runs
tables.description: Each daily check of one business's own Stripe account (arch 10 line 550: 'Daily at 03:00 UTC over the last 48 hours'): the window listed through K-14's listMoney, when it ran and finished, and how many charges and refunds it listed. One row per business and window, so a job run again after a crash writes no second run.
tables.source: arch 09 line 457 ('Stripe checked daily'); arch 10 line 550; K-14 v1 listMoney; 01-inventory C-112 reconciliation job

columns.name: id
columns.description: The run's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business whose connected account was listed. Row-level security scopes by it.
columns.source: arch 10 lines 546, 550; K-14 v1 listMoney.request account

columns.name: window_from
columns.description: The window's start, included: 48 hours before window_to (K-14 listMoney from).
columns.source: arch 10 line 550 ('over the last 48 hours'); K-14 v1 listMoney.request from

columns.name: window_to
columns.description: The window's end, left out: 03:00 UTC on the run's day (K-14 listMoney to).
columns.source: arch 10 line 550 ('Daily at 03:00 UTC'); K-14 v1 listMoney.request to

columns.name: job_id
columns.description: The job that ran it, as K-07's effects.job_id and K-04's event log name a job.
columns.source: K-07 v1 effects.job_id; K-04 v1 event_log.job_id

columns.name: started_at
columns.description: When it started.
columns.source: arch 10 line 550

columns.name: finished_at
columns.description: When it finished, every finding written; null while running or after a failed listing, which the job tries again (arch 10 line 540). Set once.
columns.source: arch 10 lines 540, 550; K-14 v1 listMoney.errors ('A partial listing is never given')

columns.name: charges_listed
columns.description: How many charges the listing gave; set once, when finished.
columns.source: K-14 v1 listMoney.response

columns.name: refunds_listed
columns.description: How many refunds the listing gave; set once, when finished.
columns.source: K-14 v1 listMoney.response

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: raised when the run finishes, compared and set by the job (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: reconciliation_runs_id_business_key
unique.source: Its findings carry its business (README rule 5)

unique.name: reconciliation_runs_one_per_window
unique.source: arch 10 line 550 (daily: one run per business and window)

checks.name: reconciliation_runs_window
checks.source: arch 10 line 550; K-14 v1 listMoney ('to ... later than from')

checks.name: reconciliation_runs_finished
checks.expression: (finished_at is null) = (charges_listed is null) and (finished_at is null) = (refunds_listed is null) and (charges_listed is null or (charges_listed >= 0 and refunds_listed >= 0)) and (finished_at is null or finished_at >= started_at)

tables.name: reconciliation_findings
tables.description: What a daily check found that did not already match, and what it did (arch 10 line 550): a charge with no line, whose line it wrote; a charge with no agreed booking behind it, refunded at once and both told (S12-26); a line with no charge, which takes the charge-failed path (A6-32); a charge or refund with no effect id, which gets no line and no refund (CQ-15's default); anything else, for Rosie's team within 1 business day (S12-24). Written once by the job, never edited.
tables.source: arch 10 line 550; S12-24; S12-26; A6-32; CQ-15; K-14 v1 listMoney; K-07 v1 effects (reconciliationJob)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The finding's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09

columns.name: run_id
columns.description: The run that found it (reconciliation_runs.id), held to the same business.
columns.source: arch 10 line 550

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The run's business. Row-level security scopes by it.
columns.source: arch 10 line 546

columns.name: kind
columns.description: line_written (a charge with no line: the line is written), refunded_at_once (a charge with no line and no agreed booking behind it: its line is written and it is refunded at once), line_without_charge (a charge line the listing does not give: the charge-failed path), no_effect_id (a listed charge or refund with no effect id: no line, no refund), other (anything else: Rosie's team).

columns.name: stripe_object_id
columns.description: The listed Stripe charge or refund it is about (K-14 listItem stripeId); null for a line with no charge.
columns.source: K-14 v1 listItem.stripeId

columns.name: effect_id
columns.description: The effect id the listed object carried, as listed (K-14 listItem effectId); null when it carried none (CQ-15).
columns.source: K-14 v1 listItem.effectId; CQ-15

columns.name: ledger_line_id
columns.description: The line written for it, or the line with no charge (ledger_lines.id), held to the same business.
columns.source: arch 10 line 550

columns.name: refund_id
columns.description: For refunded_at_once: the refund made at once (refunds.id), held to the same business.
columns.source: S12-26; K-07 v1 effects (reconciliationJob writes a stripe_refund)

columns.name: to_team
columns.description: True when it goes to Rosie's team, within 1 business day (S12-24): a listed object with no effect id, and anything else.
columns.source: arch 10 line 550 ('Anything else: Rosie's team within 1 business day'); S12-24; CQ-15

columns.name: found_at
columns.description: When it was found.
columns.source: arch 10 line 550

unique.name: reconciliation_findings_object_key
unique.source: arch 10 line 550 (each listed object found once a run: a job run again writes nothing twice)

unique.name: reconciliation_findings_line_key
unique.source: arch 10 line 550

checks.name: reconciliation_findings_fits
checks.expression: (kind <> 'line_written' or (ledger_line_id is not null and stripe_object_id is not null and refund_id is null)) and (kind <> 'refunded_at_once' or (ledger_line_id is not null and stripe_object_id is not null and refund_id is not null)) and (kind <> 'line_without_charge' or (ledger_line_id is not null and stripe_object_id is null)) and (kind <> 'no_effect_id' or (stripe_object_id is not null and effect_id is null and ledger_line_id is null and refund_id is null)) and to_team = (kind in ('no_effect_id', 'other'))

indexes.name: reconciliation_findings_team_idx
indexes.why: What went to Rosie's team, oldest first, within 1 business day (S12-24; C-194).
